A.why: A clear tiered skirt that reads from above, but all one dark green, stiffly stepped like a cake, with a square top.

B.why: Good green over straw contrast, but the short straight skirt reads as a kilt under a boxy coat and a soldier's cap.

C.why: The laced bodice is a nice idea, but a broad square torso over a short stack of flat discs reads top-heavy and blocky.

D.why: The fullest flaring plate skirt, spoiled by shoulder blocks that stand past the shoulder line and a muddy brown palette with no waist.

E.why: The only set that reads as a gown at once: an ankle-length bell of vertical reed panels with a pale V neckline, held back by heavy blocky shoulders.

notes: Every set keeps full-width blocky shoulders and sleeves and no cinched waist, so none gets the narrow-top, wide-hem outline; the reed straw and pale bone trims that would make them read at night are used too timidly.
